html:
The Chaco War was fought from 1932 to 1935 between Paraguay and Bolivia over the northern Gran Chaco, a dry thorn-forest plain. Paraguay won most of the disputed land.

Bolivia wanted a river route to the Atlantic, and both sides hoped for oil. Paraguay fought near home and moved troops by rail and river, while Bolivian soldiers from the highlands suffered terribly from heat and thirst. Paraguayan commanders such as José Félix Estigarribia won a string of victories. Tens of thousands died on both sides, many of thirst and disease. The Chaco War page tells the war in full.

A peace treaty in 1938 gave Paraguay most of the Chaco. The war made army officers powerful in both countries, and in Bolivia defeat led towards the revolution of 1952.
